work.title: Vollständiges Liederbuch der Freymäurer mit Melodieen

history.p: One of the last projects that Scheibe managed to work on was a new, heavily revised collection of communal songs for the Masons. It was published in 1776 with a dedication to the brothers dated 1764. The new collection did not only include his previously published songs of 1749 (SchW B5:Coll.004), but also new ones as well as old ones which had been performed at the Lodge’s meetings since around 1756 and which he also had composed. Furthermore, Scheibe consulted all the published collections of Freemason’s songs which he could get hold of. The purpose was to collect all the songs into one manageable edition. The work also includes an extensive and detailed introduction on both sources and approach as well as performance practice issues such as men’s voices, range, and chorus; he also explains the aesthetics of the songs in terms of simplicity and naturalness. According to Scheibe, the songs have been improved in terms of range and 'singability' and have all been added a figured bass part. Often the earlier songs or melodies were either too high or too low and were not comfortable ('Nicht der Zwang, sondern die Natur macht eine Melodie angenehm und leicht. Edle Simplicitet, wie sehr wirst du verkannt!', introd. p. xi). The songs have been emended and those which could not have been provided with a new melody or recomposed. Thus the members are provided with light and easy melodies which can be sung by all men and the volume may be carried along when visiting the Lodge. In the introduction Scheibe also promises that a second volume will appear if he finds more songs. In 1785 a second volume appeared edited by Christian Gottlob Proft and having mentioned that Scheibe issued the first volume, Proft continues: 'In this preface, he gives an account of his work which ought to be successful since he has worked with his strong point, the art of music, as well as the lighter forms of poetry. In this collection he has been working with a great many songs, both text and melodies. In his foreword, he promises the continuation of the collection and only his death very soon after has prevented him from fulfilling this promise.' Scheibe lists his sources providing a brief description of them and how they have been included in the present collection. Scheibe has assigned each song with an abbreviation indicating source and what he has done with the song.

annot.p: 'Er giebt in der Vorerinnerung Rechenschaft von seiner Arbeit, die ihm gelingen muste, da er bey seiner groβen Stärke in der Tonkunst, zugleich viel in den lichtern Dichtungsarten gearbeitet, wie denn in jene Sammlung sehr viele Lieder, beydes Text und Melodien ihm gehören. In eben der Vorerinnerung verspricht er die Fortsetzung der Sammlung, und nur seine sehr bald darauf erfolgter Tod, hat ihn an der Erfüllung dieses Versprechens gehindert'.

annot.p: According to Scheibe's introduction, this source consists of melodies that have been in use in Copenhagen for the last 20 years (i.e., since c. 1756) as well as those published by Scheibe in 1749 (SchW B5:Coll.004); they have all been included in the present collection, though improved ('verbessert').

annot.p: The editor of the present work is Theodor Gottlieb von Hippel.

According to Scheibe's introduction, this source consists of three new texts in German by Johann Elias Schlegel, which he wrote while in Copenhagen; they have been included in the present collection with new melodies by Scheibe.
